harappan_connection.value: At Qal'at al-Bahrain, the first Indus-inspired circular 'Gulf-type' stamp seals appear in layers contemporary with the city-wall construction c. 2050 BCE, some bearing short inscriptions in Indus script; simultaneously a formal weight system was adopted - cubical and spherical stone weights matching Harappan standard units, the system known in Babylonia as the 'Tilmun norm' (na Tilmun, UET 5 796). Square polished weights of Indus origin are also reported from the site.

harappan_connection.value: Sixteen Indus-style seals excavated at Ur: published by C.J. Gadd 1932 ('Seals of ancient Indian style found at Ur,' Proc. British Academy XVIII); four from the Royal Cemetery (UE 2, Woolley 1934); nine catalogued UE 10 (Legrain 1951, Cat. 624-632). UE 10's Introductory Note states they 'prove the existence of early trade relations between the Indus valley and lower Mesopotamia.'
